
### latency (1)  {.smaller}



* latency: time for message: SOURCE $\rightarrow$ DEST
* example: [1000]{.fragment fragment-index=3 .custom .myem-only} bit message from S to D:
 

::: {.r-stack}

![](/perf/texfig/latency-latency-1.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="S <--> D via 50 Mbit, 500 meters of copper" width=1000px}

![](/perf/texfig/latency-latency-1.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="S <--> D via (highlighted) 50 Mbit, 500 meters of copper" width=1000px}

![](/perf/texfig/latency-latency-1.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="S <--> D via 50 Mbit (highlighted) 500 meters of copper" width=1000px}


:::
 

* [one]{.fragment fragment-index=2 .custom .myem-only} bit sent each [1/50M second = 0.02 $\mu$ s]{.fragment fragment-index=2 .custom .myem-only}
* [1000 bits take $0.02 \times 1000 = 20\;\mu$ s to sent]{.fragment fragment-index=3 .custom .myem-only} 
   * ‘‘transmission delay’’
* + $2.2$ microseconds for bit to go down cable ($2.3\times10^8$ m/s) 
   * ‘‘propogation delay’’
* total latency of about 22.2 $\mu$ s


### latency (1, ex)  {.smaller}



![](/perf/texfig/latency-latency-1-ex.figure.svg){fig-alt="S <--> D via 1 Gbit, 10 km of fiber" width=1000px}

* exercise: latency for 20000 bit message from S to D 
   * assume speed of signal through fiber of $2.0\times10^8$ m/s



### latency (2)  {.smaller}



* example: 1000 bit packet from S to D
* assume when message is received: 
   * 5 other 1000-bit packets in queue; no extra bits between packets
   * no other switch processing time

![](/perf/texfig/latency-latency-2.figure.svg){width=1000px}

::: {.fragment}

* S to switch, switch to D: 22.2 $\mu$ s [ (transmit+propogate delay)]{.my-small}
* within switch: wait $20\times5=100\;mu$ s for 5 other packets ($20\mu s$ = 1 packet transmit delay) 
   * ‘‘queueing delay’’
* total latency: $22.2 + 100 + 22.2 = 144.4$ microseconds

:::


### round trip time 


* round-trip-time (RTT): time for message:  <br> SOURCE $\rightarrow$ DEST $\rightarrow$ SOURCE 
<hr class="vspace" />
* much easier to measure than one-way latency
* typically how we'll see latency
